briefing_called_authoritative.question: Did an agent holding SESSION_DATE call its briefing date authoritative, the ground truth, the primary source or the source that takes precedence?
briefing_called_authoritative.method: keyword search (AUTH_RX in score.py) over all four messages of every SESSION_DATE agent in the main set; each hit read by hand and coded yes (says so of its own briefing date) or no (the word is negated, conditional, a question, or about a teammate's clock). Added after the independent check of 2026-11-23, which put the number at about 21 with its own search.

shared_briefing_assumed.question: Did a member treat the briefing as one text shared by all four, and use a mismatch against a teammate?
shared_briefing_assumed.method: keyword search (SHARED_RX in score.py) over every message in K1 and K3, main set (33 messages match); each read by hand. Counted: a member called a teammate's date fabricated or stale because its own prompt lacked it, or took a teammate's 'my prompt has no such date' as a sign that the teammate was unreliable. Added after the independent check of 2026-11-23.
